Unit 8: Describing Quantitative Findings

单元八：描述量化研究结果

Student Version | Course Notes & Statistical Analysis Tasks

学生版 | 课堂笔记与统计分析任务

Professional Workplace Communication: Proposal and Report Writing (LAN4103)

专业职场沟通：提案及报告写作（LAN4103）
Vocabulary: objectively (adverb): considering only facts and without being influenced by personal feelings or opinions

Learning Objectives

学习目标

By the end of this unit, you will be able to:

学完本单元后，你将能够：
  • identify the purposes of various visuals for presenting IT statistical data
  • describe quantitative findings (distributions, pre- and post-project comparisons, changes and trends)
  • select and describe salient findings clearly and objectively in evaluation reports
识别各种视觉图表在呈报IT统计数据中的用途 | 描述量化研究结果（分布情况、项目前后比较、变化和趋势） | 在评估报告中清晰客观地选取和描述显著发现

Quantitative findings are the numerical data collected using tools such as questionnaire surveys. They are expressed in numbers, percentages, or statistics, and provide measurable evidence to assess a project's effectiveness objectively. Visuals help people see comparisons, relationships, or trends clearly.

量化研究结果是使用问卷调查等工具收集的数值数据，以数字、百分比或统计数据表示，提供可量化的证据以客观评估项目成效。视觉图表有助于人们清晰地看到比较、关系或趋势。

Task 1: Presenting Statistical Data

任务一：呈报统计数据

Match each visual type to its appropriate purpose:

将每种视觉图表与其适当用途配对：
Visual TypeAppropriate Purpose (Match A–E)
1. Pie chart
2. Bar chart
3. Line graph
4. Table
5. Pictogram

Task 2a: Describing Distributions

任务二a：描述分布情况
Sample Formula: [General description] + [Segment description] + [Conjunction] + [Numerical description] + [Segment description]
Example: "More than half of the respondents checked their online systems for potential threats on a weekly basis, whereas 16% of them did so monthly."
描述饼图或百分比分布时，可将数字描述（如60%）与概括描述（如「超过半数受访者」）结合使用。

Reporting Grammatical Adjustments:

报告时的语法调整：
  • 'you' → 'respondents' / 'participants'
  • 'check' → 'checked' (simple past tense)
  • 'your' → 'their'
  • 'did so' to avoid repeating the full phrase

Practice 1:

Survey: "How often do you run anti-virus scans?"

Daily: 55% | Twice weekly: 37% | Weekly: 8% | Never: 0%

Practice 2:

Survey: "How often do you review website security certificates?"

Very often: 97% | Quite often: 3% | Occasionally: 0%

Task 2b: Describing Pre- and Post-Project Findings

任务二b：描述项目前后的结果
Example 1: "More than half of the respondents checked their online systems for potential threats on a weekly basis, which was a significant improvement from only 2% before the project."
Example 2: "About one-third of them did so every two weeks, compared to 10% prior to the project."
项目前后数据通过比较干预前后的态度或习惯来衡量影响。

Practice 1:

"How often do you test the firewall configuration?"

Once a month: Pre 0% → Post 5% | Once in three months: Pre 5% → Post 60% | Once in six months: Pre 10% → Post 25% | Never: Pre 85% → Post 10%

Practice 2:

"Do you agree that regular password resets are necessary to prevent data leakage?"

Disagree: Pre 96% → Post 0% | Somewhat agree: Pre 4% → Post 60% | Strongly agree: Pre 0% → Post 40%

Practice 3:

"Are you satisfied with the performance of the new AI agent?"

Very satisfied: Pre 7% → Post 75% | Satisfied: Pre 30% → Post 20% | Not satisfied: Pre 63% → Post 5%

Task 2c: Describing Changes and Trends

任务二c：描述变化和趋势
Trend Analysis Examples:
• "The percentage of clients who agreed that the prices of anti-virus software products were fair rose sharply from 23% two years ago to 77% this year."
• "The percentage of shoppers who thought the interface of our online store was poor fell remarkably from 97% to 17%."
• "The percentage of customers who wanted more product tutorials remained stable over the past three years (45% → 46% → 45%)."
• Contrast: "The number of respondents who ran anti-virus scans 'quite often' increased sharply from 5% to 90%, while those running scans 'occasionally' dropped significantly from 95% to 7%."
趋势分析范例：使用上升/下降动词（如rise、drop）搭配程度副词（如sharply、remarkably）来描述变化。用contrast连接词（如while、whereas）对比不同趋势。

Task 3: Reporting Salient Findings

任务三：报告显著发现
Vocabulary: salient (adjective): most important; noticeable or prominent

It is not necessary to report every detail. Select only the most salient findings to keep your evaluation focused and impactful. Highlight key changes such as a significant rise or decline, or major contrasts that demonstrate project impact.

无需报告每个细节。只选取最重要的研究结果，使评估聚焦且有影响力。突出显示关键变化，如显著的上升或下降，或展示项目影响的重大对比。

Case Scenarios — Identify the salient findings:

i. Challenges faced in adopting VR tools: [Lack of staff training] and [Limited integration with existing systems], accounting for the overwhelming majority of obstacles.

ii. Firewall implementation across 4 office networks (Security attacks Pre vs Post):

Office A: 17 → 16 | Office B: 28 → 2 | Office C: 32 → 19 | Office D: 47 → 47

iii. IDS deployment across network segments (Cyber threats without vs with IDS):

Segment A: 46 → 37 | Segment B: 22 → 21 | Segment C: 18 → 0 | Segment D: 4 → 5

iv. Cloud collaboration tool staff logins across departments:

Sales: 53 | R&D: 104 | Finance: 131 | HR: 178

任务四：撰写评估报告（第二部分——量化研究结果）

Project: 'Data Analytics Basics for Nonprofits'

Survey Data:

  • Q1 Familiarity with data analytics tools: Very familiar (Pre 12% → Post 26%), Familiar (Pre 5% → Post 68%), Quite familiar (Pre 10% → Post 6%), Not at all (Pre 73% → Post 0%)
  • Q2 Confidence in creating basic data visualisations: Highly confident (Pre 5% → Post 15%), Fairly confident (Pre 15% → Post 80%), Not at all (Pre 80% → Post 5%)

Unit 9: Describing Qualitative Findings

单元九：描述质性研究结果

Professional Workplace Communication: Proposal and Report Writing (LAN4103)

专业职场沟通：提案及报告写作（LAN4103）
Vocabulary: qualitative (adjective): relating to what something is like or how good it is, rather than how much of it there is

While quantitative data provides measurable evidence of an IT project's outcomes, qualitative data reveals the reasons and user perspectives behind system adoption and performance. Reporting qualitative findings complements metrics with human insights.

量化数据提供项目成果的可量化证据，而质性数据（意见、开放式回答、访谈）则揭示数据背后的原因和洞察。你将学习报告质性研究结果，以人文视角补充数据驱动的结果。

Task 1: Analysing Qualitative Data (Categorisation)

任务一：分析质性数据（分类）

Classify each comment as Positive, Negative, or Irrelevant based on tone and relevance to the 'CyberSecure HK' project:

根据语气和与「CyberSecure HK」项目的相关性，将每条评论分类为正面、负面或无关：

A. 'The hands-on practice with real-world scenarios was incredibly helpful.'

B. 'Absolutely disappointed! No advanced tools are covered in the workshops.'

C. 'The real-world scenarios about phishing are so relatable.'

D. 'The examples provided were highly relevant to my daily work.'

E. 'No support outside the workshops! I feel completely abandoned!'

F. 'I love the cybersecurity tools introduced. They are all very useful.'

G. 'I have to push back my schedule just to attend the workshop.'

H. 'I had to park my car far away from the training centre.'

Task 2: Reporting Positive Comments

任务二：报告正面评价
Three-Step Thematic Process:
1. Group comments into common themes → 2. Identify significant themes → 3. Summarise and report key insights
三步主题分析法：1. 将评论归类为主题；2. 识别重要主题；3. 总结并报告关键洞察。

Key Themes Identified from Focus Group:

  • Theme 1: High relevance of real-world cybersecurity scenarios (e.g. phishing simulations)
  • Theme 2: Practical utility of security tools (e.g. two-factor authentication)

Reporting Key Insights using Reported Speech:

a. Real-world scenarios: "It was commented that the real-world phishing scenarios were highly relevant to participants' daily work."

b. Security tools: "Some participants were satisfied with the usefulness of the cybersecurity tools, noting that two-factor authentication effectively enhanced device protection."

Task 2b: Practice — Reporting VR Workshop Comments

任务二b：练习——报告VR体验工作坊评价

1. 'The workshop was really engaging! The immersive VR experience is truly transformative.'

2. 'I am interested in learning more about VR technology.'

3. 'The instructor clearly explained how the VR works and the step-by-step guidance is easy to understand.'

Task 3: Reporting Negative Comments Tactfully

任务三：委婉报告负面评价
To provide a balanced evaluation, negative comments must be reported to pinpoint areas for improvement. Use neutral, professional, and constructive language rather than harsh or critical wording.
为提供平衡的评估，必须报告负面评论以指出改进领域。使用中立、专业和建设性的语言，而非严厉或批评性的措辞。

Comparison:

  • Harsh: "No support outside the workshops! I feel completely abandoned!"
  • Version A (Direct): "Some expressed that there was no support outside the workshops. They felt completely abandoned."
  • Version B (Tactful & Constructive): "Some thought the learning process would be more effective with additional support outside the workshops."

Techniques:

TechniqueDirect / Rude FeedbackTactful Reporting
1. Replace rude/offensive words with neutral terms'The course fees are a complete RIP-OFF!'Some students thought that the digital audio production course fees were somewhat high.
2. Focus on the issue, not the person'The instructor spoke so fast; I couldn't follow the steps.'Feedback indicated that the instruction pace was quite fast, making certain technical steps difficult to follow.
3. Use frequency words to show non-constant issues'If I can't book a digital audio workstation through the online system, how am I supposed to practise?'It was reported that users occasionally experienced difficulties booking digital audio workstations through the online system.
4. Highlight constructive elements'The front desk was a disaster! The staff were so rude when I asked about schedules!'Feedback revealed that customer service communication at the front desk could be improved.

Task 3c: Practice — Rewriting Negative VR Comments Tactfully

任务三c：练习——委婉改写VR体验负面评价

1. 'We waited too long for our turn to try on the VR headsets.'

2. 'The handouts were poorly written and didn't match what we were taught in the workshop.'

3. 'The VR headset kept crashing, which made the training pointless and confusing!'

Task 4: Completing an Evaluation Report (Part III — Qualitative Findings)

任务四：完成评估报告（第三部分——质性研究结果）
CA Assessment: This task mirrors the EAII exam format. Draft Section 3 (cont'd) incorporating qualitative feedback tactfully.
此任务模拟EAII考试格式。请巧妙地将质性反馈纳入报告第三部分（续）。

Focus Group Feedback from 'Data Analytics Basics for Nonprofits':

  • Positive: 'The real-world dataset exercises are highly practical and easy to understand. Fantastic! 😊'
  • Constructive: 'My device was too outdated for running the data analytical tools, so the hands-on exercises were quite frustrating. 🙁'
  • Negative (Emotional): 'Totally IRRELEVANT! No non-profit data or examples? What a complete waste of time! 😡'

3. Findings (cont'd) — Qualitative Feedback

Task 1: Mobile Game Development Basics

任务一：手机游戏开发基础
You are Angel Chan, a project assistant at InnoTech Education Institute. You have conducted a mini-project to teach teenagers foundational skills in mobile game design and programming through hands-on workshops. You are required to write an evaluation report to your supervisor discussing the effectiveness of the project and giving recommendations for the way forward. Using the notes and data you have compiled, complete the evaluation report with appropriate elaboration.
你是InnoTech Education Institute的项目助理Angel Chan。你开展了一个迷你项目，通过实践工作坊教授青少年手机游戏设计和编程的基础技能。你需要向主管撰写评估报告，讨论项目成效并提出改进建议。

Evaluation report on the 'Mobile Game Development Basics' project

1. Introduction

The booming mobile gaming industry has sparked teenagers' interest in game development. Despite this growing enthusiasm, many lack the technical knowledge and creative skills needed to design functional and engaging games. The objective of the 'Mobile Game Development Basics' project is to teach teenagers foundational skills in game design, programming, and problem-solving through hands-on workshops. This report assesses the effectiveness of the project and provides suggestions for future improvement.

蓬勃发展的手机游戏行业激发了青少年对游戏开发的兴趣。尽管热情高涨，但许多人缺乏设计功能性和吸引力游戏所需的技术知识和创意技能。「手机游戏开发基础」项目的目标是通过实践工作坊教授青少年游戏设计、编程和问题解决的基础技能。本报告评估项目成效并为未来改进提供建议。

2. Methodology

2.1 Participants

Three professional game developers were recruited as trainers, while 40 teenagers from various secondary schools in Hong Kong were invited to participate in the project.

三名专业游戏开发者获聘为培训师，40名来自香港各中学的青少年受邀参加项目。

2.2 Implementation

From January to February 202-, five workshops were conducted by the trainers. These sessions covered topics such as coding basics using the Unity game engine, designing user interfaces, implementing game mechanics, and testing functionality. Participants engaged in practical exercises, including prototyping simple games and troubleshooting common issues.

一月至二月期间，培训师举办了五节工作坊。课程涵盖使用Unity游戏引擎的编程基础、用户界面设计、游戏机制实现和功能测试等主题。参与者进行了实践练习，包括制作简单游戏原型和排除常见问题。

2.3 Evaluation

To evaluate the project, participants had been invited to complete a pre-project survey in December 202- assessing their prior knowledge of game development. In March 202-, a post-project survey was administered, and online group discussions were held to gather feedback on their experiences and challenges faced during the workshops.

为评估项目，参与者于十二月完成了评估其游戏开发先验知识的项目前调查。三月进行了项目后调查，并举办了线上小组讨论以收集他们在工作坊期间的体验和挑战反馈。

Evaluation Report on 'Cantonese for All' Project

1. Introduction

The non-Chinese speaking (NCS) students who are new to Hong Kong often face challenges in integrating due to language barriers. The mini-project, 'Cantonese for All', aims to help these students learn Cantonese to improve their daily interactions and community integration. This report discusses the effectiveness of the project and provides recommendations for future initiatives.

新来的非华语学生因语言障碍往往面临融入社区的挑战。「人人学广东话」迷你项目旨在帮助这些学生学习广东话，改善日常交流和社区融合。本报告讨论项目成效并为未来活动提供建议。

2. Methodology

2.1 Participants

Two instructors were recruited to deliver the course, while 50 new NCS students from Hong Kong Higher Institute were invited to participate in the course.

两名导师获聘授课，50名来自香港专上学院的新非华语学生受邀参加课程。

2.2 Implementation

From October to November 202-, twelve 1-hour lessons were conducted by the instructors. These lessons focused on teaching the NCS students useful daily Cantonese expressions, such as greetings, ordering food, and asking for directions, in addition to some highlights of local culture.

十月至十一月期间，导师共举办了十二节一小时的课程。课程重点教授非华语学生实用的日常广东话表达，如问候、点餐和问路，同时介绍本地文化亮点。

2.3 Evaluation

To collect data for evaluation, the NCS students completed a pre-project survey in September 202-. In December, they took part in a post-project survey and focus group interviews to share their experiences.

为收集评估数据，非华语学生于九月完成了项目前调查。十二月，他们参加了项目后调查和焦点小组访谈，分享他们的体验。

  1. Findings
  2. Discussion
  3. Conclusion
  4. Recommendations

Report Part I: 1. Introduction

报告第一部分：1. 引言

Evaluation Report on ‘Impact and Success of V-Music Library’ Project

「V-Music Library的影响与成效」项目评估报告

1. Introduction 简介

Music education and access to the music industry are important for young musicians. Yet many young musicians lack platforms to showcase their work and connect with industry professionals V1. This mini-project, ‘Impact and Success of V-Music Library’, evaluated the newly launched V-Music Library and its contribution to music education and industry engagement among HKDI students and alumni V2. The report considers participants’ self-reported confidence using digital music tools and motivation to collaborate, together with their feedback on library resources, networking opportunities and ease of use V3. It discusses the project’s effectiveness and makes recommendations for its future development.

音乐教育及接触音乐业界对培育年轻音乐人十分重要。然而，许多年轻音乐人缺乏展示作品及与业界人士联系的平台。此迷你项目「V-Music Library的影响与成效」评估新推出的V-Music Library对HKDI学生及校友的音乐教育及业界参与有何贡献。本报告探讨参与者对使用数字音乐工具的自我评估信心、与其他音乐人合作的动力，以及他们对馆藏资源、交流机会和平台易用性的意见，并据此讨论项目成效及提出未来发展建议。
Clues to reuse: background need V1 → project purpose V2 → evaluation focus V3. The later sections should return to these aims and use the actual findings as evidence. 可重用线索：背景需要 V1 → 项目目的 V2 → 评估重点 V3。后续部分须呼应这些目标，并以实际结果为依据。

Report Part I: 2. Methodology

报告第一部分：2. 研究方法

2. Methodology 研究方法

2.1 Participants 参与者

Six students were recruited as researchers, while 40 HKDI students and alumni participated in the project’s surveys, interviews and workshops.

六名学生获招募为研究员；40名HKDI学生及校友参与项目的调查、访谈及工作坊。

2.2 Implementation 实施

From October to November 202-, the student researchers took part in vinyl-record workshops, observed mini-concerts, interviewed V-Music Library participants and staff, and examined visitor engagement at the “Timeless Ideas & Icons” exhibition V4.

202-年10月至11月，学生研究员参加黑胶唱片工作坊、观察迷你音乐会、访问V-Music Library的参与者及职员，并考察「Timeless Ideas & Icons」展览期间的访客参与情况。

2.3 Evaluation 评估

A pre-project survey was conducted in September 202-, followed by a post-project survey in December. The survey asked about confidence using digital music tools such as DAWs and samplers, and whether the Library motivated respondents to collaborate with other musicians. Focus-group interviews in December collected participants’ views and experiences V3V5.

项目于202-年9月进行项目前调查，并于12月进行项目后调查。问卷询问参与者使用DAW及采样器等数字音乐工具的信心，以及V-Music Library有否激励他们与其他音乐人合作。12月举行焦点小组访谈，收集参与者的意见及体验。
Interpret the evidence carefully: these are self-reported before-and-after results and focus-group comments. They show perceived change and user experience; the notes do not establish that the Library alone caused the changes or that motivation led to completed collaborations. 解读证据时须谨慎：这些是项目前后自我评估结果及焦点小组意见，反映参与者感受到的变化和使用体验；现有资料未能证明变化单由图书馆造成，亦未证明合作动力已转化为实际合作。

6. Recommendations

3.1 Quantitative Findings: Template → Output (Blanks 1–12)

3.1 量化研究结果：模板 → 输出（空格1–12）

Use the numbered fill-in template at the end of the final tab. Red circles show blank numbers; orange circles mark added explanation. 请使用最后一个标签末页的编号填空模板。红色圆圈表示空格编号；橙色圆圈表示补充说明。

Q2 · Motivation to collaborate
Template pattern: After the project, [1] reported that they [2], compared with [3] before. The share who [4] reported that they [5] was lower than [6] before.
模板句式：项目结束后，[1]表示他们[2]，而项目前为[3]。表示[4]的比例较项目前[6]的[5]有所下降。
Output: After the project, three-quarters of respondents1 reported that they felt motivated to collaborate with other musicians2, compared with 5%3 before. Likewise, just 2%4 reported that they were not motivated to collaborate5, down from 80%6 before the project.
输出：项目结束后，四分之三的受访者表示他们有动力与其他音乐人合作，项目前则为5%。同样，项目后仅2%表示没有合作动力，较项目前的80%为低。
Q1 · Confidence using digital music tools
Template pattern: The number of respondents who [7] rose from [8] to [9], while those who [10] fell from [11] to [12].
模板句式：表示[7]的受访者人数由[8]上升至[9]；表示[10]的人数则由[11]下降至[12]。
Output: The proportion of respondents who felt slightly confident using DAWs and samplers7 rose from 22%8 to 69%9, while those who were not confident using digital music tools10 fell from 64%11 to 2%12.
输出：对使用DAW及采样器稍有信心的受访者比例由22%升至69%；对使用数字音乐工具没有信心的比例则由64%降至2%。
Writing tip: “rose from … to …” and “fell from … to …” make the direction of change clear. These are percentage-point differences, not percentage growth rates. 写作提示：「由……升至……」及「由……降至……」清楚交代变化方向。这里比较的是百分点差异，并非百分比增长率。

Pedagogical Analysis 教学分析

  • Report the salient changes rather than listing every response category; the source notes ask students to highlight only key points.
    只报告重点变化，不必逐一列出所有选项；题目笔记要求突出重点。

  • Describe these as before-and-after self-reports. The pattern is consistent with improvement during the project, but does not by itself prove causation.
    将其描述为项目前后的自我评估。数据变化与项目期间的改善相符，但单凭这些数据不能证明因果关系。

3.2 Qualitative Findings: Template → Output (Blanks 13–15)

3.2 质性研究结果：模板 → 输出（空格13–15）

Use the shared template on the final tab. Keep the tone neutral and attribute opinions to participants.请使用最后一个标签的共用模板；语气保持中立，并将意见归于参与者。

Positive comment
Template pattern: It was also found that … [13].
Output: It was also found that the Library’s rare vinyl records had inspired some participants’ composition styles13.
输出：研究亦发现，图书馆的珍稀黑胶唱片启发了部分参与者的作曲风格。
Concern and suggestion
Template pattern: However, some respondents mentioned that … [14]. Furthermore, some suggested that … [15].
Output: However, some participants said that they wanted more networking events with producers and artists14. Furthermore, some expressed concern that the interface was confusing and difficult to use15.
输出：然而，部分参与者表示希望增加与制作人及艺人的交流活动。此外，部分参与者担心界面令人困惑、难以使用。
Writing tip: “some participants said…” reports a view without presenting it as everyone’s experience. Rephrase emotional wording in a respectful, professional tone. 写作提示：「部分参与者表示……」可避免把个别意见说成所有人的体验；应以尊重、专业的语气改写情绪化措辞。

3.2 Qualitative Findings: Data Sources & Analysis

3.2 质性研究结果：数据来源及分析

The source is the three comments recorded from focus-group interviews. They illustrate experiences; they do not establish how common each view was.资料来自焦点小组访谈记录的三项意见。这些意见说明参与者的体验，但不能显示每种看法有多普遍。

Blank / evidenceCareful report wordingWhat it may indicateLimit
13 Rare vinyls inspired composition; “treasure trove”Some participants said the rare vinyls inspired their composition styles.Music resources can support creative exploration.One positive comment does not measure learning gains.
14 Wants more networking eventsSome participants wanted more events with producers and artists.Industry contact remains an area to strengthen.A request is not proof that no networking occurred.
15 Interface confusing and hard to useSome participants found the interface difficult to navigate.Usability may limit access to resources.The comments do not identify which features caused difficulty.
Language move: keep the observation (“participants found…”) separate from the interpretation (“this may indicate…”). 语言技巧：将观察（「参与者认为……」）与诠释（「这可能表示……」）分开。

Part 1 · Project outcome

The proportion who felt slightly confident rose from 22% to 69%, while the proportion reporting no confidence fell from 64% to 2%.

Part 2 · Resource and collaboration experience
Template: Moreover, students have benefited from [18], which [19]. [Elaboration]
模板：此外，学生受惠于[18]，这[19]。[详细说明]
Output: Moreover, students have benefited from access to the Library’s rare vinyl collectionV5, which participants said had inspired their composition stylesV5. Respondents also reported greater motivation to collaborate after the project, although some still wanted more events with producers and artists.
输出：此外，学生受惠于图书馆的珍稀黑胶唱片馆藏；参与者表示这些唱片启发了他们的作曲风格。受访者亦表示项目后更有动力合作，但部分人仍希望增加与制作人及艺人的交流活动。
Interpretation check: say “motivation to collaborate increased”; do not change this into “students built collaborative networks” unless the report supplies evidence of actual collaboration. 诠释检查：应写「合作动力上升」；除非报告提供实际合作的证据，否则不可改写成「学生建立了合作网络」。

3.3 Discussion: Data Sources & Analysis

3.3 讨论：数据来源及分析

Pedagogical Analysis: Trace the Clues and the Limits 教学分析：追踪线索及证据界限

Tap or hover a tagged phrase to see its source and how it was adapted. Hide the tags to try first.点击或悬停带标签的词句，查看线索来源及改写方式；可先隐藏标签自行尝试。

Sources to reuse: Introduction, Methodology and focus-group feedback 可重用资料：引言、研究方法及焦点小组意见
Evidence chain: project purpose V2 + measured self-reported change V3 + user comments V5 → a qualified discussion. V4 gives implementation context, but the notes do not connect a specific activity to each survey change. 证据链：项目目的 V2 + 自我评估变化 V3 + 使用者意见 V5 → 谨慎讨论。V4提供实施背景，但资料未把某项活动与每项调查变化直接对应。
  • Paraphrase aims as outcomes, but keep claims proportionate to what was measured.
    将目标改写为成果，但论断须符合实际测量内容。
  • Use “suggests” or “was associated with”; the before-and-after design does not establish causation.
    使用「显示」或「与……相关」；项目前后比较不能证明因果关系。
  • Distinguish motivation from behaviour: the survey measures willingness to collaborate, not completed collaborations.
    区分动力与行为：问卷测量合作意愿，并非实际完成的合作。

3.4 Conclusion: Template → Output (Blank 20)

3.4 结论：模板 → 输出（空格20）

The conclusion returns to the Introduction’s purpose and summarizes only findings already discussed.结论呼应引言的目的，并只概括前文已讨论的发现。

Conclusion
Template: To conclude, the project has been successful/effective in [20]. While similar projects should continue to be offered, there are some areas that could be improved for better results.
模板：总括而言，项目成功／有效地[20]。虽然应继续推行类似项目，但仍有部分地方可予改善，以取得更佳成果。
Output: To conclude, available evidence suggests that the project has been effective in supporting music education through inspiring resources and strengthening self-reported confidence with digital tools and motivation to collaborateV2V3V520. While similar projects should continue to be offered, networking opportunities and interface usability should be improved.
输出：总括而言，现有证据显示该项目有效支持音乐教育：提供启发创作的资源，并提升参与者对数字工具使用信心及合作动力的自我评估。虽然应继续推行类似项目，但仍须改善交流机会及界面易用性。
Alternative: “promoting music learning, encouraging creative exploration and increasing participants’ reported willingness to collaborate.” Keep parallel -ing forms after “effective in”. 其他写法：「促进音乐学习、鼓励创意探索，并提高参与者自述的合作意愿。」“effective in”之后保持平行的 -ing 形式。

3.4 Conclusion: Data Sources & Analysis

3.4 结论：数据来源及分析

Pedagogical Analysis: Conclusion as a Bookend of the Introduction 教学分析：结论与引言首尾呼应

Introduction purpose
Support music education and industry engagement; provide access to music resources and connection.
支持音乐教育及业界参与；提供音乐资源及交流机会。
⇄
Conclusion (20)
Summarize the reported changes in digital-tool confidence and collaboration motivation, plus the value of rare vinyl resources.
总结数字工具使用信心和合作动力的变化，以及珍稀黑胶资源的价值。
Conclusion claimEvidence to reuseBoundary
More confidence using toolsSlightly confident: 22% → 69%; not confident: 64% → 2%Self-reported confidence, not assessed skill.
More motivation to collaborate“Yes”: 5% → 75%; feedback still requested more events.Motivation is not proof of actual networking.
Creative resource valueFeedback says rare vinyls inspired composition style.A comment illustrates experience; it does not quantify impact.
Bookend rule: the Introduction gives the purpose; the conclusion states what the evidence suggests was achieved and what remains incomplete. Do not introduce new findings or claim causation. 首尾呼应：引言交代目的；结论总结证据显示哪些目标可能达成、哪些仍未完成。不要加入新发现或声称因果关系。

Discussion

  • Survey responses show higher reported familiarity with AR/AI and greater inspiration to explore creative tools after the festival. They are self-reports, not a technical-knowledge test. Blanks 16–17
  • Interactive experiences may support engagement and exploration. The AR demo comment is a positive example; comments also identify barriers for beginners. Blanks 18–19

Conclusion

  • Summarize reported familiarity and inspiration changes, while noting that before-and-after responses do not prove the festival caused them. Blank 20

Recommendations

  • Beginner-friendly guides and interactive tutorials respond to the technical-level concern. Blank 21
  • Simplified content is supported by comments about technical difficulty. Multilingual support is a useful proposal, but no language-specific need is documented; check attendee preferences. Blank 22
  • Visual aids and glossary handouts directly address jargon in expert talks. Blank 23
写作笔记。讨论：项目前后调查显示参与者对AR／AI的自述熟悉程度及探索创意广告工具的动力有所上升；这不是技术知识测验。互动体验可能有助参与及探索；一项AR示范意见是正面例子，另有意见指出初学者面对的障碍。结论须总结自述变化并说明不能证明因果。建议：以初学者指南及互动教程回应技术门槛；简化内容。多语言支援可作为建议，但没有记录具体语言需要，应先了解参加者偏好；视觉辅助及词汇表可回应专家讲座中的行话问题。

Report Part I: 1. Introduction

报告第一部分：1. 引言

Evaluation Report on ‘AdTech Festival: Future of Advertising’ Project

AdTech Festival：广告的未来 项目评估报告

1. Introduction 简介

As advertising technologies such as AR, AI-generated content and programmatic media become more popular, public interest in these tools is growing D1. Yet opportunities for the public to learn how these technologies work and are used may be limited. The mini-project, ‘AdTech Festival: Future of Advertising’, responded by offering a three-day public festival of exhibits, demonstrations, expert talks and workshops to raise awareness D2. This report evaluates the festival’s effectiveness and recommends improvements for future festivals D3.

随着AR、AI生成内容及程序化媒体等广告科技日渐普及，公众对这些科技的兴趣亦不断增加。然而，公众了解这些科技的运作及用途的机会可能有限。迷你项目「AdTech Festival: Future of Advertising」透过举办为期三天的公众节庆活动，包括展品、示范、专家讲座及工作坊，回应这方面的需要并提高公众认识。本报告评估节庆活动的成效，并为未来活动提出改进建议。
Clues to reuse: growing popularity and public interest D1 provide the context; the possible lack of learning opportunities helps explain the awareness aim. Festival activities D2 show how the project addressed that aim. Use the survey and focus-group evidence D3 to evaluate the project and support the Discussion, Conclusion and Recommendations. 可重用线索：科技日渐普及及公众兴趣上升 D1 提供背景；公众学习机会可能有限，说明提高认识的目标。节庆活动 D2 显示项目如何回应此目标。运用问卷及焦点小组证据 D3 评估项目，并支持讨论、结论及建议。

Report Part I: 2. Methodology

报告第一部分：2. 研究方法

2. Methodology 研究方法

2.1 Participants and setting 参与者及场地

The three-day festival was held at HKDI Gallery and brought together industry experts, creative professionals and more than 200 public attendees.

为期三天的节庆活动在HKDI Gallery举行，汇聚业界专家、创意专业人士及200多名公众参加者。

2.2 Implementation 实施

From October to November 202-, the team curated content, invited speakers, prepared the venue and ran promotional campaigns. The public festival included an exhibition and workshop series with interactive exhibits, demonstrations and expert talks. The project brief identifies AR, AI-generated content and programmatic media as areas of public interest, and a participant specifically praised an AR demo. The project also included post-event media coverage D4.

202-年10月至11月，团队策划内容、邀请讲者、布置场地并进行宣传。公开节庆活动包括展览及工作坊系列，以互动展品、示范及专家讲座介绍AR、AI生成内容及程序化媒体等主题。活动后的媒体报道让项目讯息延伸至场外。

2.3 Evaluation 评估

A pre-project survey was conducted in September 202- and a post-project survey in December. The survey asked how familiar participants were with AR and AI and whether the festival inspired them to explore creative advertising tools. Focus-group interviews collected comments on the exhibits and expert talks D3D5.

项目于202-年9月进行项目前调查，并于12月进行项目后调查。问卷询问参与者对AR及AI的熟悉程度，以及节庆活动有否启发他们探索创意广告工具。焦点小组访谈则收集参与者对展品及专家讲座的意见。
Evidence limit: the notes report more than 200 attendees but do not state how many completed each survey. These are before-and-after self-reports and focus-group comments; no control group, significance test or follow-up measure is supplied. Describe a pattern consistent with increased familiarity or interest, not proven causation or lasting learning. 证据限制：笔记记载参加者超过200人，但没有说明各次调查的实际回应人数。这些是项目前后自我评估及焦点小组意见；资料没有对照组、显著性检验或后续追踪测量。应描述与熟悉程度或兴趣增加相符的变化，不可声称因果关系或长期学习效果已获证实。

3.1 Quantitative Findings: Template → Output (Blanks 1–12)

3.1 量化研究结果：模板 → 输出（空格1–12）

Use the AdVision source map on the template slide. Red circles show blank numbers; describe changes in percentage points and avoid claiming statistical significance.请参照模板页的AdVision资料对照。红色圆圈表示空格编号；以百分点描述变化，不要声称统计显著。

Q1 · Familiarity with AR and AI
Template pattern: After the project, [1] said they [2], compared with [3] before. [4] reported that they [5], compared with [6] before.
Output: After the project, 62%1 of respondents reported that they were familiar with advertising technologies such as AR and AI2, compared with approximately one-fifth (21%)3 before. A further 27%4 said that they were highly familiar with these technologies5, compared with 3%6 before the festival.
输出：节庆活动结束后，62%的受访者表示熟悉AR及AI等广告科技，项目前约为五分之一（21%）。另有27%表示非常熟悉，项目前则为3%。
Q2 · Inspiration to explore creative tools
Template pattern: The proportion who [7] rose from [8] to [9], while those who [10] fell from [11] to [12].
Output: The proportion of respondents who were very inspired to explore creative advertising tools7 rose from 5%8 to 77%9, while those who were not inspired at all10 fell from 82%11 to 2%12.

Writing tip: 77% were “very” inspired and 21% “quite” inspired after the festival, so 98% reported at least some inspiration. Do not write 93%. “Marked rise” is safer than “statistically significant increase” because no significance test is provided. 写作提示：节庆活动后，77%表示「非常」受启发，21%表示「颇受」启发，合计98%表示至少受到一些启发。不可写成93%。资料没有显著性检验，因此「明显上升」比「统计上显著增加」稳妥。

Clues to reuse: Introduction, Implementation and Evaluation 可重用线索：引言、实施及评估
Evidence chain: public interest D1 → awareness aim D2 → festival activities D4 → familiarity/inspiration measures D3 D5 → qualified discussion. The evidence supports reported change and positive experience; it does not prove causation or lasting learning. 证据链：公众兴趣 D1 → 提高认识的目标 D2 → 节庆活动 D4 → 熟悉程度／启发程度指标 D3、D5 → 谨慎讨论。证据支持自述变化及正面体验，但不能证明因果关系或长期学习效果。
  • Use activities as context for why the outcomes may have changed; do not state that a specific exhibit caused a survey result unless measured.

Pedagogical Analysis: Conclusion as a Bookend of the Introduction

教学分析：结论与引言首尾呼应
Introduction purpose
Raise public awareness of emerging advertising technologies and invite the public to explore them.
提高公众对新兴广告科技的认识，并邀请公众探索相关科技。

Conclusion (20)
Summarize the reported familiarity and inspiration changes, then identify accessibility as the remaining issue.
总结熟悉程度及启发程度的自述变化，并指出内容易读性仍须改善。
Conclusion pointEvidenceBoundary
Greater familiarityFamiliar/highly familiar: 24% before → 89% afterSurvey response; respondent count not reported.
Greater inspirationVery/quite inspired: 18% before → 98% afterSelf-reported inspiration, not later tool use.
Memorable experienceOne participant said the AR demo helped them learn immersive branding.An example comment, not an audience-wide measure.
Improvement neededComments mention technical exhibits for beginners and jargon in talks.Qualitative comments do not show prevalence.
Bookend rule: return to the awareness aim in the Introduction, state what the results suggest, and preserve the limits of self-reported pre/post data. Do not add claims about long-term learning or behaviour. 首尾呼应：回到引言的提高认识目标，说明结果显示什么，并保留项目前后自我评估的限制。不要加入长期学习或行为方面的论断。

Evaluation Report: 1. Introduction

评估报告：1. 引言

Evaluation report on ‘Data Analytics Basics for Nonprofits’ project

「非营利机构数据分析基础」项目评估报告

As the importance of data analytics continues to grow in today’s data-centric world, many local non-profit organisations in Hong Kong find themselves lacking the necessary skills to harness data for organisational growth. This mini-project, ‘Data Analytics Basics for Nonprofits’, sets out to improve their understanding of data analytics and provide them with practical skills by introducing basic analytical tools and techniques. This report evaluates the project’s effectiveness and offers recommendations for future enhancements.

随着数据分析在当今以数据为本的世界中日益重要，香港不少本地非营利机构发现自己缺乏善用数据以推动机构发展所需的技能。这个小型项目「非营利机构数据分析基础」旨在通过介绍基础分析工具和技巧，加深他们对数据分析的理解，并为他们提供实用技能。本报告评估项目的成效，并就日后的改进提出建议。
The highlighted parts show the key information you will reuse in the Discussion, Conclusion and Recommendations.
高亮部分是你在讨论、结论及建议部分将会再用到的关键信息。

Evaluation Report: 2. Methodology

评估报告：2. 研究方法

2.1 Participants

2.1 参加者

Four IT students were recruited as instructors, while 25 local non-profit organisations were invited to join the project.

招募了四名IT学生担任导师，并邀请25家本地非营利机构参加项目。

2.2 Implementation

2.2 实施

From January to February 202-, five online workshops were conducted by the instructors, during which they demonstrated how to use spreadsheet functions, interpret simple data visualisations, and apply basic statistical methods. Participants also engaged in hands-on exercises using real datasets.

于202-年一月至二月，导师举办了五场网上工作坊，示范如何使用电子表格函数、解读简单的数据可视化图表及应用基本统计方法。参加者亦参与了使用真实数据集的实践练习。

2.3 Evaluation

2.3 评估

To gather evaluation data, participants were asked to complete a pre-project survey in December 202- on data analytics and visualisation. In March 202-, a post-project survey was conducted, and virtual focus group discussions were held to collect feedback and review participants’ experiences.

为收集评估数据，参加者于202-年十二月须完成一份关于数据分析及可视化的项目前问卷调查。202-年三月进行了项目后问卷调查，并举行了网上焦点小组讨论，以收集反馈及回顾参加者的体验。

3.1 Quantitative Findings: Data Sources & Analysis

3.1 量化研究结果：数据来源及分析

Pedagogical Analysis

教学分析
  • General Numerical Expressions: Rather than merely reporting raw percentages, the output uses academic approximations (‘slightly more than two-thirds’ for 68% at (1); ‘approximately a quarter’ for 26% at (4)), as the template prompts.
    一般数字表达：不只是列出原始百分比，而是运用学术性的约数表达（68%写成“略多于三分之二”，26%写成“约四分之一”），符合模板提示。
  • Template Stems Followed Strictly: Each sentence keeps the template’s fixed stems (‘After the project…’, ‘compared to … before’, ‘Moreover, the number of respondents who…’, ‘while those … fell’); only the numbered blanks are filled, and trend words come from the template’s options (‘a significant increase’, ‘rose sharply’, ‘fell drastically’).
    严格沿用模板句式：每句均保留模板固定句式（“After the project…”、“compared to … before”、“Moreover, the number of respondents who…”、“while those … fell”），只填写有编号的空格；趋势用语取自模板选项（“a significant increase”、“rose sharply”、“fell drastically”）。
  • Reported Speech & Pronoun Cohesion: ‘said that they were…’ and ‘reported that they were very familiar with them’ use reported speech, and ‘them’ refers back to ‘data analytics tools’ to avoid repetition.
    转述句与代词衔接：“said that they were…”及“reported that they were very familiar with them”使用转述句，代词“them”指代“data analytics tools”，避免重复。

3.2 Qualitative Findings: Data Sources & Analysis

3.2 质性研究结果：数据来源及分析

Pedagogical Analysis

教学分析
  • Constructive Rephrasing of Raw Feedback: The raw comment at (15), ‘Totally IRRELEVANT! No non-profit data or examples? What a complete waste of time!’, is neutralised into ‘some of them suggested that more data and examples specific to non-profit organisations should be used’, following the teacher’s asterisk rule.
    把原始反馈改为建设性表达：(15)的原始评论为“完全不相关！没有非营利机构的数据或例子？简直浪费时间！”，按教师的星号规则中和为“部分受访者建议使用更多针对非营利机构的数据和例子”。
  • Diplomatic Problem Articulation: At (14), ‘quite frustrating’ becomes the formal ‘faced issues with outdated devices … which hindered their learning experience’.
    委婉地陈述问题：(14)中的“相当令人沮丧”改为正式表达“遇到设备过时的问题……影响了学习体验”。
  • Template Stems & Transition Markers: ‘It was also found that’, ‘However, some respondents mentioned that’ and ‘Furthermore, some of them suggested that’ introduce the positive point, the problem and the suggestion in turn.
    模板句式与过渡词：“It was also found that”、“However, some respondents mentioned that”及“Furthermore, some of them suggested that”依次引出正面意见、问题及建议。

Informed decisionsA1
⇢
Operational efficiencyinferred: keep the claim modest

Solid = traceable to the clues; dashed = the writer’s inference (it comes from the meeting notes, not the Introduction or Implementation). 实线＝可追溯至线索；虚线＝作者的推断（来自会议记录）。

  • Expanding Short Meeting Notes: the notes become a causal chain: workshops → tool skills → everyday behaviours → operational efficiency.
    扩展简短的会议记录：被整合为因果链：工作坊→工具技能→日常行为→营运效率。
  • Evaluative Wording: ‘effectively’, ‘evidently’ and ‘enhanced’ create a confident tone, but ‘The findings suggest’ is hedged. Use strong words only where the findings support them.
    评价性用语：“effectively”“evidently”“enhanced”营造自信语气，但“The findings suggest”属保守表述；只有在数据支持时才使用强烈用语。
  • Tense shift: the Methodology reports what was done (past: ‘were conducted’, ‘demonstrated’); the Discussion reports results with present relevance (‘have boosted’, ‘now regularly analyse’).
    时态转换：研究方法用过去时描述所做之事；讨论用现在完成时／一般现在时描述仍有影响的成果。
  • Avoid: copying the Introduction word for word (e.g. repeating ‘lacking skills’), claiming more than the evidence shows, or mixing tenses.
    避免：逐字照抄引言（如重复“缺乏技能”）、夸大证据、混用时态。
Before you write each elaboration, ask: (1) Which Implementation activity caused this? (2) Which Introduction need does it answer? (3) Have I paraphrased it?
撰写每个详细说明前先问：(1) 是哪项实施活动带来这个结果？(2) 它回应引言中的哪项需要？(3) 我有没有改写？

Conclusion

Output: To conclude, the project has been effective in boosting participants’ data analytics capabilities and empowering them to make data-driven decisions20. While similar projects should continue to be offered, there are some areas that could be improved for better results.

Pedagogical Analysis (A): Conclusion as a Bookend of the Introduction

Clues to reuse: Introduction (slide 103) and Implementation (slide 104) 可重用的线索：引言（幻灯片103）及实施（幻灯片104）
Introduction aim (slide 103)
‘to improve their understanding of data analytics and provide them with practical skills’

⇄
Conclusion (20)
The project has been effective in boosting participants’ data analytics capabilitiesA2 and empowering them to make data-driven decisionsA1A3.

  • The Conclusion restates the aim as an achievement and adds no new information. Pair the words: improve understanding → boosting … capabilities; provide practical skills → empowering … to make decisions.

  • After ‘effective in’, keep parallel -ing forms (boosting … and empowering …).

加入与非营利机构相关的个案研究／使用针对非营利机构的个案研究／采用来自非营利界别的个案研究

Pedagogical Analysis (B): Recommendations: Clue → Evidence → Action

教学分析（乙）：建议：线索 → 实证 → 行动

The three recommendations are not generic: each starts from what the project did, is backed by evidence, and ends with an action. 三项建议并非泛泛而谈：从项目所做之事出发，有实证支持，并落实为行动。

Language Focus 语言重点
